newsitem.title: POLAND: Warsaw streetcar gives driver the slip.
newsitem.headline: Warsaw streetcar gives driver the slip.

text.p: A tram escaped from its terminal and sped driverless for several kilometres (miles) through the centre of the Polish capital before dawn on Wednesday before jumping the rails and demolishing a flower shop.

PAP news agency quoted a Warsaw city transport spokesman saying the motorman had just got out to walk to the other end of the two-carriage streetcar when it took off backwards down the track, defying all efforts to halt it.

"The terminal crew switched off the power at several substations, but momentum kept the tram going at a probable speed of about 30 km (18 miles) an hour," spokesman Andrzej Wisniewski told the agency.
Private Radio Zet said tram staff frantically gave chase in a small car through the largely deserted streets.
The runaway finally crossed a junction at speed, causing it to jump the track and destroy a florist's concrete booth.
Wisniewski said initial theories were that a short-circuit in the steering system may have prompted the incident, in which no one was hurt.
